data.short_meaning: Remembrer, One who keeps the faith alive
data.long_meaning: The name Munthir is derived from the Arabic root 'n-th-r', which means to remember or keep in mind. This name is often given to those who are diligent in their faith and are constantly reminding themselves and others of Allah and His teachings. In the Quran, the Prophet Ibrahim (as) is referred to as a 'Munthi', meaning one who is constantly remembering and calling upon Allah.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder and a source of guidance

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Munthir total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Munthir ibn Sanan, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), was known for his excellent memory and was entrusted with the transmission of many Hadiths. He is mentioned in several Hadiths and was also one of the scribes who recorded the Hadiths for future generations.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, era of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

historical_references.reference: Al-Munthir bin Abdulwadud, a prominent scholar and jurist of the Maliki school of Islamic law, lived during the 10th and 11th centuries. He was born in Morocco and studied under several notable scholars of his time. His works include commentaries on Imam Malik's Al-Muwatta' and Al-Mudawwana, as well as a collection of Hadiths called Al-Jami' al-Kabir.
